title: What is the question asking?
goal: Before you look for an answer, say the question's job: what kind of answer, about what, and how many parts.

card.title: KIND – ABOUT – HOW MANY
lines: KIND: what kind of answer does it want?
HOW MANY: how many parts do I need?
Flip words: NOT and EXCEPT turn the question around.

kinds.thing: a thing (an object, a problem or an idea)
kinds.purpose: what a part of the text is for

kind.person: Who wants a person or a group.
kind.thing: What wants a thing: an object, a problem or an idea.
kind.action: 'What did someone do' wants something someone did.
kind.words: 'What did someone say' or 'text' wants the words.
kind.reason: Why wants a reason. A reason starts with 'because'.
kind.way: How wants a way of doing something.
kind.amount: How much, how many and how long want an amount.
kind.choice: Which wants one choice from the list.
kind.sentence: 'Which sentence' wants a sentence you can point to in the text.
kind.purpose: 'Purpose' asks what that part of the text is for.

about.topic: That is the topic. The target is longer. Read everything after the question word.
about.other: That is about something else. Read the question again, word by word.
about.otherPart: That is the other part of the question. Find the 'and', then look at this part only.

feedback.parts: Look for 'and' joining two questions. Count again.
feedback.flipMissed: Look again. One small word flips this question.
feedback.flipNone: No flip word here. The flip words are NOT and EXCEPT.
feedback.flipMeaning: A flip word turns the job around. Most choices will be true. You are hunting for the one that is not.

levels.description: Correct answer in a complete sentence.
Correct answer, but not a complete sentence.
Incorrect, or does not answer the question.
Both parts answered correctly, in complete sentences.
Both parts answered correctly but not in complete sentences, or one part correct in a complete sentence.
One part answered correctly, not a complete sentence.

last-bus.title: The Last Bus
sentences: Priya finished her shift at the pizza place at 10:40 p.m.
The last bus left at 10:55, and the stop was a ten-minute walk away.
She pulled on her jacket, said goodnight to her manager, and walked fast.
Halfway there, her phone buzzed.
It was her little brother: "Mom's asking where you are."
Priya typed "On my way" without slowing down.
When she turned the corner, the bus was already at the stop with its doors open.
She broke into a run, waving one arm.
The driver saw her in the mirror and waited.
Priya climbed on, breathing hard, and dropped into the first empty seat.
"Thanks," she said.
The driver just nodded.
As the bus pulled away, Priya looked at the dark street behind her and let out a long breath.
She made a note on her phone: Ask for the 9 p.m. shift next week.
last-bus.tutorNote: This story is also used in the paper diagnostic. Assign Module 1 only after the diagnostic has been done.

vending.title: The Vending Machine
sentences: The vending machine outside the gym ate Daniel's two dollars on Monday.
He pressed the button for a water, the coil turned, and the bottle stuck against the glass.
He hit the side of the machine twice.
Nothing.
The next day he brought a note to the office with the machine's number on it.
On Friday, a man in a grey uniform refilled the machine and left an envelope with Daniel's name on it at the front desk.

sections.title: The trick
sections.tutorNote: I DO. Read the explanation together, do the matching, then reveal the worked example one step at a time while thinking aloud.

text: Before you look for the answer, say the job in three pieces.
KIND: what kind of thing am I looking for?
HOW MANY: how many things do I need?
If you can say the job, you can find the answer. If you can't say the job, you're guessing.

steps.prompt: Match each question word to the kind of answer it wants.

pairs.right: a thing, something that happened, or an idea
a way of doing something, or an amount

steps.title: Watch one

reveals.label: Flip word?
reveals.text: No NOT or EXCEPT. Nothing flips.

reveals.label: First question word
reveals.text: WHY. Why wants a reason. About what? About the driver waiting.

reveals.label: Keep reading
reveals.text: There is an AND. After it: HOW did she thank him. How wants a way of doing something. About Priya thanking him.

reveals.label: The job
reveals.text: One reason the driver waited, and one way Priya thanked him. Two parts.

reveals.label: Now look at the story
reveals.text: Reason: the driver saw her. Way: she said thanks. The job told me what to look for.

steps.question: Why did the driver wait for Priya, and how did she thank him?
